im-c64-01.h: -고 보니 (완료 후 발견) vs -다 보니 (진행 중 깨달음) vs -다 보면 (미래 예측)

a.d: Action was finished, and only afterwards was a surprising truth discovered.
ex: 음식을 다 **먹고 보니** 그릇 밑에 머리카락이 있었어요. — After finishing all the food, I realized there was a hair under the bowl.

b.d: Engaging repeatedly in an action over time naturally led to a habit, result, or understanding.
ex: 한국 친구들과 매일 **이야기하다 보니** 말하기 실력이 부쩍 늘었어요. — Through constantly talking with Korean friends, my speaking skills improved remarkably.

im-c64-01.tip: -고 보니 is for a single finished action. -다 보니 is for accumulated experience. -다 보면 looks to the future: "if you keep doing it, you will see..." (연습하다 보면 잘하게 돼요).

im-c64-01.hint: Use continuous cumulative experience marker -다 보니: 살다 보니.
im-c64-01.why: Living over an extended period represents cumulative ongoing experience, requiring -다 보니.

im-c64-02.h: -더니 (남의 변화 관찰) vs -았/었더니 (내가 직접 해본 경험의 결과)

a.d: The speaker witnessed another person’s action or past weather, which led to a contrast or change.
ex: 친구가 어제 밤새 게임을 **하더니** 오늘 수업 시간에 졸고 있어요. — My friend played games all night yesterday, and now is nodding off in class.

b.d: The speaker personally performed the action in the 1st person, resulting in a discovery, reaction, or consequence.
ex: 아침에 따뜻한 차를 **마셨더니** 감기 기운이 한결 가라앉았어요. — I drank warm tea in the morning, and my cold symptoms subsided noticeably.

im-c64-02.tip: Check the subject: Use -았/었더니 when "I" did the action (내가 했더니). Use -더니 when observing others or weather changes (친구가 열심히 하더니, 어제 춥더니).

im-c64-02.q: Fix the subject mismatch where a 1st-person action was written with the 3rd-person observer ending.

answers: 제가 어제 운동을 무리해서 했더니 오늘 온몸이 쑤셔요.
제가 어제 운동을 무리해서 했더니 오늘 온몸이 쑤셔요

im-c64-02.why: The subject is 1st person (제가), so the direct experiential result marker -았/었더니 must be used.

im-c64-03.h: -다가는 (위험한 미래 경고) vs -(으)ㄴ/는 셈이다 (사실상의 종합 평가)

a.d: Warns that if current negative behavior continues, a disastrous outcome will inevitably follow.
ex: 그렇게 과속을 **하다가는** 큰 사고가 날 수 있어요. — If you keep speeding like that, a terrible accident could happen.

b.d: Concludes that, taking everything into account, the situation practically amounts to a certain result.
ex: 목표의 구십 퍼센트를 달성했으니 이번 프로젝트는 **성공한 셈이에요**. — Having achieved ninety percent of targets, this project is practically a success.

im-c64-03.tip: Use -다가는 to urgently caution against reckless habits. Use -(으)ㄴ/는 셈이다 to deliver balanced summaries of achievements or costs.

a.d: States results without revealing the underlying discovery process or experiential depth.
ex: 운동하니까 좋아요. 계속하세요. — Exercise is good. Keep doing it.

b.h: 깊이 있는 통찰 전달 (Insightful experiential narrative)
b.d: Articulates how repeated practice (-다 보니), direct trials (-았/었더니), and warnings (-다가는) combine for profound wisdom.
ex: 무리하게 운동하**다가는** 다치기 쉽지만, 매일 조금씩 하**다 보면** 체력이 부쩍 늘어난 것을 실감하게 돼요. — While over-exercising risks injury, if you keep doing a little daily, you will feel your stamina noticeably expanding.

im-c64-04.tip: Synthesizing trial outcomes (-고 보니), gradual adaptation (-다 보니), and realistic warnings (-다가는) creates persuasive essays and mentoring advice.
